scope: Source-review and clear the four held Passport candidates (QED, Yang-Mills, GKSL/Lindblad, quantum error correction), correcting only their declared formula provenance/metadata and adding one authoritative modern-QED notation source. Existing 25 Passports and unrelated scientific/runtime records are preserved.

before.name: QED Lagrangian
before.plain: L_QED = psi-bar(i hbar c gamma D - mc^2)psi - F^2/4
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: QED Lagrangian
after.plain: L_QED = -F_mn F^mn/4 + psi-bar(i gamma^mu D_mu - m)psi
after.description: Gauge-invariant spinor QED Lagrangian in natural units before gauge fixing.
assumptions: One Dirac matter field coupled minimally to an Abelian U(1) gauge field in the displayed representative.
Natural units hbar=c=1; D_mu psi = (partial_mu + i e A_mu)psi and F_mu nu = partial_mu A_nu - partial_nu A_mu.
Gauge-fixing and ghost terms are absent from the displayed gauge-invariant classical Lagrangian; perturbative quantization requires a gauge choice.
The compact modern notation is source-locked to Tong's course notes rather than attributed verbatim to the 1949 Feynman/Dyson papers.
after.regime: Relativistic spinor quantum electrodynamics in the standard U(1) formulation. The displayed action defines the theory but does not by itself solve strong-field, bound-state or nonperturbative observables.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1; restore constants only after choosing a consistent unit convention for both matter and gauge terms.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 6.3, Eq. (6.67) / HTML Eq. (6.559), with D_mu=partial_mu+i e A_mu; Sec. 6.4 repeats the QED Lagrangian

after.name: Dirac Feynman propagator
after.description: Momentum-space propagator of a free Dirac fermion in natural units.
assumptions: Free Dirac-field propagator used as the internal fermion line of perturbative QED.
Natural units hbar=c=1 and metric/sign conventions are those of the cited QFT notes.
The Feynman i epsilon prescription fixes the time-ordered boundary condition.
after.regime: Free Dirac propagator and perturbative-QED internal line; self-energy corrections replace the free propagator in interacting resummed descriptions.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 5.5, Eq. (5.35), momentum-space factor i(gamma dot p + m)/(p^2-m^2+i epsilon); repeated in Sec. 6.5 QED Feynman rules

before.name: Yang–Mills field strength
before.plain: F^a_mn = d_m A^a_n - d_n A^a_m + g f^abc A^b_m A^c_n
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Yang–Mills field strength
after.plain: F^a_mn = d_m A^a_n - d_n A^a_m + g f^abc A^b_m A^c_n
after.description: Modern Lie-algebra notation for the non-Abelian field strength; Yang and Mills wrote the original SU(2) case in isotopic-vector/matrix notation.
assumptions: Gauge potential A_mu=A_mu^a T^a takes values in a Lie algebra with [T^a,T^b]=i f^{abc}T^c under the displayed convention.
The sign of the nonlinear term follows D_mu=partial_mu+i g A_mu; changing generator or covariant-derivative conventions can flip signs or move factors of g.
Yang and Mills (1954) explicitly treat the SU(2) isotopic-spin case; the displayed f^{abc} form is its standard modern generalization.
after.regime: Classical local non-Abelian gauge field before gauge fixing/quantization. This identity alone does not establish confinement or a mass gap.
after.units: Natural-unit gauge-theory convention; dimensions depend on spacetime dimension and field normalization.

sourceLocations.locator: Phys. Rev. 96, pp. 192–193, Eqs. (4)–(9): SU(2) matrix/isotopic-vector gauge field and nonlinear field strength; modern structure-constant notation is a declared generalization

before.name: Yang–Mills Lagrangian
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.

after.name: Yang–Mills Lagrangian
after.description: Pure non-Abelian gauge-field Lagrangian in standard modern normalization.
assumptions: Pure gauge sector only; matter fields and gauge-fixing/ghost terms are not included.
Generator normalization is absorbed into the component normalization giving the conventional -1/4 coefficient.
The original Yang–Mills paper uses SU(2) isotopic-vector conventions; the displayed compact component formula is a modern normalization of the same gauge-field kinetic structure.
variables: g: coupling contained in F_mu nu^a through the chosen convention
after.regime: Classical pure Yang–Mills action and starting point for quantized non-Abelian gauge theory; the Lagrangian alone is not a proof of confinement, a mass gap or QCD phenomenology.
after.units: Natural units with conventional four-dimensional field normalization.

sourceLocations.locator: Phys. Rev. 96, p. 193, Eq. (11) with the field-strength definitions developed in Eqs. (4)–(9); modern -1/4 F^a_mu nu F^{a mu nu} notation is convention-normalized

before.name: GKSL/Lindblad master equation
before.description: General Markovian completely positive trace-preserving semigroup generator.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: GKSL/Lindblad master equation
after.description: Schrödinger-picture GKSL generator for a norm-continuous completely positive trace-preserving quantum dynamical semigroup, with positive rates shown explicitly.
assumptions: Time-homogeneous quantum dynamical semigroup (Markovian semigroup) rather than general non-Markovian evolution.
Bounded/norm-continuous generator in Lindblad's theorem; finite-dimensional systems satisfy the boundedness condition automatically.
gamma_k >= 0; factors sqrt(gamma_k) can equivalently be absorbed into Lindblad operators.
Trace preservation is encoded by the anticommutator terms and complete positivity by the GKSL structure.
after.regime: Uniformly/norm-continuous CPTP semigroup dynamics. Time-dependent, memory-kernel and general non-Markovian equations are outside the theorem's semigroup scope.
after.units: H has energy units; gamma_k has inverse-time units if L_k is dimensionless; hbar is displayed explicitly in the Hamiltonian term.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical Schrödinger-picture form equivalent to the bounded-generator GKSL theorem

sourceLocations.locator: Commun. Math. Phys. 48, 119–130 (1976), Theorem 2, Eqs. (4.2)–(4.3), p. 128: bounded generator and dual Schrödinger-picture form
J. Math. Phys. 17, 821–825 (1976): general generator of completely positive dynamical semigroups for finite N-level systems

before.name: Knill–Laflamme error-correction condition
before.plain: P Ea† Eb P = c_ab P
before.description: Condition for a code subspace to exactly correct a set of errors.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Knill–Laflamme error-correction condition
after.plain: P Ea† Eb P = c_ab P
after.description: Basis-independent projector form of the necessary and sufficient exact quantum error-correction conditions for a specified error set.
assumptions: P projects onto the chosen code subspace and {E_a} is the specified set/span of correctable interaction/error operators.
c_ab is independent of the encoded logical state; equivalently E_a^dagger E_b acts as a scalar on the code subspace.
The condition is for exact subspace quantum error correction, not approximate correction, fault-tolerance thresholds or a claim that arbitrary errors are correctable.
variables: P: projector onto the code subspace
E_a,E_b: error/interaction operators in the correctable set
c_ab: scalar Hermitian matrix over error labels
after.regime: Exact subspace quantum error correction for a declared error set/channel operator span. Approximate/operator-algebra QEC use generalized conditions.
after.theoryRelationship: necessary and sufficient exact recovery condition in compact projector form

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:quant-ph/9604034v1, Sec. 2 Eqs. (6)–(7), PDF pp. 5–6; Sec. 3 formalizes the necessary/sufficient recovery conditions. P E_a†E_b P=c_ab P is the basis-independent rewrite.

before.name: Stabilizer-state condition
before.description: A stabilizer state or code lies in the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of its stabilizer generators.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Stabilizer-state condition
after.description: A stabilizer state or code lies in the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of its stabilizer generators.
assumptions: S is an Abelian subgroup of the n-qubit Pauli group that does not contain -I for a nonempty code space.
Code states are simultaneous +1 eigenstates of every stabilizer element; it is sufficient to impose the condition on an independent generating set.
This characterizes stabilizer codes, an important subclass of quantum error-correcting codes, not all QEC codes.
variables: |psi>: code state fixed by all stabilizer generators
after.regime: Qubit stabilizer-code formalism. Nonadditive, bosonic and other non-stabilizer codes require different structures.
after.theoryRelationship: defining common +1 eigenspace condition for stabilizer codes

sourceLocations.locator: Gottesman thesis (1997), Ch. 3 Sec. 3.2, general stabilizer code: codewords are the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of the Abelian stabilizer group
